formatNotes: Eighth CrossFit Games, third at the StubHub Center. Qualification ran through the worldwide Open (a record 209,585 registrants) and 17 Regionals. 43 men and 42 women started (the official leaderboard API lists totalCompetitors 43 for women, but Rory Long-Zambard appears unranked with an overall score of 0 and no score in any of the 13 events, confirming she did not start; the other 42 women all have recorded scores). 13 separately scored individual events: The Beach at Hermosa Beach Pier and a 1-rep-max overhead squat on Wednesday, July 23, then nothing Thursday (Masters and team day), three days of competition Friday through Sunday. Most events were worth up to 100 placement points; the two Sprint Sled races were worth 50 points each. All athletes competed through Event 11 (Midline March), after which only the top 30 men and top 30 women advanced to the final two tennis-stadium events, Thick 'n Quick and Double Grace, run back to back with 2 minutes between them. The Clean Speed Ladder introduced a new bracket format: quarterfinal (top 24 advance), semifinal (top 8 advance) and final, with athletes ranked by how far they advanced and their ladder time or heaviest clean. Wanda Brenton withdrew after Event 2, Albert-Dominic Larouche after Event 6, Pip Malone after Event 10, and Kara Webb and Nicole Holcomb after Event 11.
yearSummary: 2014 was the year Rich Froning was finally pushed deep into Sunday and still won, claiming a fourth consecutive title (925 points) over 24-year-old rookie Mat Fraser (875), with Jason Khalipa third. Camille Leblanc-Bazinet broke through for her first title (918) over Annie Thorisdottir, returning from a back injury year, with med-school student Julie Foucher third. The programming opened with the longest Games swim yet (1,000 yards of ocean at Hermosa Beach inside a triplet with kettlebell thrusters and sand burpees) and a spectator-friendly Wednesday-night 1-rep-max overhead squat, where Froning and Fraser tied at 377 lb. Friday's Triple 3 (3k row, 300 double-unders, 3-mile run) handed Froning a 37th-place finish, the worst of his Games career, before he stormed back to win five of the last eight events, including the famous Push Pull duel he narrowly lost to Josh Bridges and the surprise Double Grace finale he won. New tests included the aerodynamic Sprint Sled (two 50-point pure sprint races), kettlebell thrusters, the cylinder/sandbag Sprint Carry, and the bracket-style Clean Speed Ladder won by Neal Maddox and Elisabeth Akinwale. The field was cut to 30 after Midline March, keeping the late-weekend cut introduced in recent years.

events.name: The Beach
events.description:
For time:
Swim 250 yards
50 kettlebell thrusters (35 / 24 lb.)
30 burpees
Swim 500 yards
30 burpees
50 kettlebell thrusters (35 / 24 lb.)
Swim 250 yards
Contested Wednesday morning, July 23, in the ocean at the Hermosa Beach Pier. 1,000 total yards of open-water swimming around buoys, with the thrusters and burpees performed on the sand at the waterline. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: Fourth straight year the Games opened in the water and the longest Games swim to date (1,000 yards, vs. 500 yards in the 2013 Pool, 700 m at 2012 Pendleton and 210 m at 2011 Santa Monica). Women's winner Anna Tunnicliffe (listed as Anna Tobias on the current leaderboard) is a 2008 Olympic sailing gold medalist. Rich Froning was 8th (35:10.11); Camille Leblanc-Bazinet 6th (35:58.54). Sources conflict on whether the thrusters used one or two kettlebells: Breaking Muscle's pre-event analysis described double-kettlebell thrusters, while the official card lists only '50 kettlebell thrusters (35 / 24 lb.)'.

events.name: Overhead Squat
events.description:
1-rep-max overhead squat.
Athletes each had 3 attempts to establish a maximum, choosing their own weights with increments as small as 1 lb.
Contested Wednesday evening, July 23, in the tennis stadium. Worth 100 points; scored by heaviest successful lift.
events.notes: First event announced for 2014 (revealed July 9, two weeks early). Froning and Fraser tied at 377 lb and both received the full 100 points. Kara Webb's (now Kara Saunders) 250 lb beat eventual champion Camille Leblanc-Bazinet's 242 lb by 8 lb. Wanda Brenton withdrew from the competition after this event.

events.name: Triple 3
events.description:
For time:
Row 3,000 meters
300 double-unders
Run 3 miles
Contested Friday morning, July 25, staged outside the track and soccer stadium; the 3-mile run looped around the StubHub Center grounds. Athletes competed in one large heat per division. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: Rich Froning finished 37th (38:31.38), the worst Games event finish of his career to that point; he walked portions of the run. Triple 3 became a repeated Games test in later years. Australian Rob Forte and Norwegian Kristin Holte took the wins.

events.name: Sprint Sled 1
events.description:
Sled push for time (100 yards men / 60 yards women).
Athletes pushed the new aerodynamic Sprint Sled straight down the soccer-stadium field; the official card lists no sled weight.
Time cap: 2 minutes.
Contested Friday afternoon, July 25. Worth 50 points.
events.notes: The Sprint Sled was announced as the 'first piece of new equipment for 2014.' Sled weight is stored as null because sources conflict and the official card lists no weight: Wikipedia and WODwell list a 90-lb sled with 100/60-yard distances for men/women, the official pre-Games announcement said both events were '100-yard sled pushes,' and Rogue's equipment page describes the men's sled rigged with a 35-lb C-70 bar plus two 60-lb drums and the women's with a 25-lb C-63 bar plus two 45-lb drums. One of two 50-point events run back to back.

events.name: Sprint Sled 2
events.description:
Sled push for time (100 yards men / 60 yards women).
Same course and sled as Sprint Sled 1, contested as a second, separately scored effort shortly afterward.
Time cap: 3 minutes.
Contested Friday afternoon, July 25. Worth 50 points.
events.notes: Winning times more than doubled versus Sprint Sled 1 (Maddox :30.33 to 1:09.89) because the second race was run on already-fatigued legs minutes after the first; the time cap was extended from 2 to 3 minutes. Neal Maddox swept both sled events. The official card lists no equipment change between Sled 1 and Sled 2, and lists no sled weight; sled weight is stored as null because sources conflict (Wikipedia/WODwell say 90 lb for both divisions, while Rogue's equipment page describes differently rigged men's and women's sleds - see Sprint Sled 1 notes).

events.name: 21-15-9 Complex
events.description:
For time:
8 deadlifts (155 / 115 lb.)
7 cleans (155 / 115 lb.)
6 snatches (155 / 115 lb.)
8 pull-ups
7 chest-to-bar pull-ups
6 bar muscle-ups
6 deadlifts (155 / 115 lb.)
5 cleans (155 / 115 lb.)
4 snatches (155 / 115 lb.)
6 pull-ups
5 chest-to-bar pull-ups
4 bar muscle-ups
4 deadlifts (155 / 115 lb.)
3 cleans (155 / 115 lb.)
2 snatches (155 / 115 lb.)
4 pull-ups
3 chest-to-bar pull-ups
2 bar muscle-ups
Time cap: 7 minutes.
Each round totals 21, then 15, then 9 reps on both the barbell complex (deadlift/clean/snatch) and the pull-up bar complex (pull-up/chest-to-bar/bar muscle-up). Contested Friday evening, July 25, in the tennis stadium. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: Announced by Dave Castro the same day it was contested. The eventual champions, Froning and Leblanc-Bazinet, both won this event under the Friday-night lights. Albert-Dominic Larouche withdrew after this event.

events.name: Muscle-Up Biathlon
events.description:
For time:
400-meter run
18 muscle-ups
400-meter run
15 muscle-ups
400-meter run
12 muscle-ups
Penalty: each time the athlete breaks a set of muscle-ups, they must immediately run a 200-meter lap before resuming.
Time cap: 18 minutes.
Contested Saturday afternoon, July 26, in the soccer stadium. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: Biathlon-style penalty-lap format. Rookie and former gymnast Cody Anderson famously went unbroken on all 45 ring muscle-ups to win; Froning finished 13th. Camille Leblanc-Bazinet was 2nd for the women (16:09.26) behind Tiffany Hendrickson.

events.name: Sprint Carry
events.description:
For time:
Sprint 100 yards
100-yard carry (100 / 60 lb. cylinder)
Sprint 100 yards
100-yard carry (120 / 80 lb. sandbag)
Sprint 100 yards
100-yard carry (150 / 100 lb. cylinder)
Down-and-back 100-yard shuttles across the soccer field: an unloaded sprint out, then carry an increasingly heavy object back, three times through.
Contested Saturday afternoon, July 26, in the soccer stadium. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: The pre-Games announcement listed the carries heaviest-first (150-lb cylinder, sandbag, 100-lb cylinder), but the event was contested with ascending loads as shown on the official workout archive and described by Wikipedia ('increasingly heavy objects'). Lauren Brooks doubled up after her Sprint Sled 1 win; Froning finished 15th.

events.name: Clean Speed Ladder
events.description:
Three-round elimination bracket; athletes ranked by their time to complete each ladder, or by the heaviest weight cleaned.
Quarterfinal round, for time:
1 squat clean (245 / 155 lb.)
1 squat clean (255 / 160 lb.)
1 squat clean (265 / 165 lb.)
1 squat clean (270 / 170 lb.)
1 squat clean (275 / 175 lb.)
Time cap: 2 minutes. Top 24 athletes advance.
Semifinal round, for time:
1 squat clean (280 / 180 lb.)
1 squat clean (290 / 185 lb.)
1 squat clean (300 / 190 lb.)
1 squat clean (305 / 195 lb.)
1 squat clean (310 / 200 lb.)
Time cap: 3 minutes. Top 8 athletes advance.
Final round, for time:
1 squat clean (315 / 205 lb.)
1 squat clean (325 / 210 lb.)
1 squat clean (335 / 215 lb.)
1 squat clean (340 / 220 lb.)
1 squat clean (345 / 225 lb.)
Time cap: 4 minutes.
Contested Saturday evening, July 26, in the tennis stadium. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: New advancement format for 2014: placement determined by bracket progression, then ladder speed/heaviest clean within each round, so the leaderboard records placement points rather than a time (winners display as '1 pt'). The three rounds were separately clocked elimination rounds run in heats with per-round caps of 2, 3 and 4 minutes (official card), so timeCapMin stores the 9-minute sum per the schema convention; timeDomain derives from that total window because no winning time was published. Final-round winning times were not published on the leaderboard. Neal Maddox took his third event win of the weekend; Elisabeth Akinwale won the women's final. A contemporary blog credited Scott Panchik with the men's win, but the official leaderboard shows Maddox 1st and the final barbells ended at 345/225 lb.

events.name: Push Pull
events.description:
For time:
7 handstand push-ups (deficit for men; no deficit for women in round 1)
50-foot sled pull
8 deficit handstand push-ups
50-foot sled pull
9 deficit handstand push-ups
50-foot sled pull
10 deficit handstand push-ups
50-foot sled pull
All handstand push-ups strict (no kipping). Each round the deficit increases and the sled gets heavier; the sled is pulled in hand over hand by rope. Per BarBend, sled pull loads per round were 204/260/315/370 lb. for men and 145/180/215/250 lb. for women, and the men's final-round deficit was 10 inches.
Time cap: 11 minutes.
Contested Saturday evening, July 26, in the tennis stadium. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: One of the most famous head-to-head battles in Games history: Bridges went unbroken on the final 10 deficit HSPU and held off a charging Froning on the last two sled pulls to win by about 2 seconds (4:46.43 to Froning's 4:48). Michele Letendre won the women's race by roughly 10 seconds over Nicole Holcomb. Exact HSPU deficits per round (other than the men's 10-in. final round) were not published on the official card; the official description says only that the deficit increases each round. The event was re-tested as 'Push Pull 2014 2.0' at the 2021 West Coast Classic Semifinal.

events.name: Midline March
events.description:
3 rounds for time of:
25 GHD sit-ups
50-ft. handstand walk
50-ft. overhead walking lunge (155 / 115 lb.)
Contested Sunday afternoon, July 27, in the soccer stadium by the full remaining field. Worth 100 points. The field was cut to the top 30 men and top 30 women after this event.
events.notes: Announced July 19, before the Games began. Kara Webb (Saunders) struggled badly here and withdrew from the competition afterward on medical grounds; Nicole Holcomb also withdrew after this event. Froning's win opened his five-event Sunday; Annie Thorisdottir's win kept her title hopes alive.

events.name: Thick 'n Quick
events.description:
For time:
4 rope climbs
3 overhead squats (245 / 165 lb.)
Time cap: 4 minutes.
The rope climbs were performed on thicker-than-standard ropes (hence the name), approximately 20 feet per Wikipedia. Contested Sunday afternoon, July 27, in the tennis stadium by the post-cut top 30 only. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: Women's winner Jenn Jones appears as Jennifer Astle on the current leaderboard (married name). Froning's win was his fifth consecutive Sunday event win dating back to 2013. Rope height/thickness specifics were not on the official card; Wikipedia describes 20-foot climbs on a thicker rope. Athletes then had 2 minutes before the final event began.

events.name: Double Grace
events.description:
For time:
60 clean and jerks (135 / 95 lb.)
Time cap: 7 minutes.
A doubled version of the benchmark 'Grace' (30 clean and jerks). Kept secret until the floor: the official announcement said only that athletes would face 'an unknown event, revealed to them on the floor,' and it began 2 minutes after the Thick 'n Quick time cap. Contested Sunday afternoon, July 27, in the tennis stadium by the top 30 only. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: Grace was the final event of the 2008 Games; doubling it closed 2014. Froning won the event to seal his fourth consecutive title, finishing the weekend with wins in the last three events; Annie Thorisdottir's win secured second overall behind Camille Leblanc-Bazinet. Wikipedia says the workout was announced about 30 seconds before the start.
